findings.title: Withdrawal, veil, and refuge form a protected boundary
findings.claim: Within the supplied Mary pericope, the refuge utterance is the verbal continuation of a protected-boundary sequence: withdrawal to one side, a screen, remoteness, and interior enclosure meet the request to seek shelter from the appearing figure.
findings.mechanism: The 19:16 carriers name one-sided withdrawal and a sun-facing setting, 19:17 carries the access-blocking screen, and 19:22 repeats withdrawal at a far side. Those contextual carriers activate the focus forms of refuge and protected attachment, so the focus request functions as a boundary that moves into speech when spatial separation no longer suffices.
findings.reader_payoff: The appeal can be read as an action inside an already constructed enclosure: the reader sees distance, screening, and refuge as connected operations rather than as isolated narrative details.
findings.containment: The primary reading remains Mary seeking refuge in the Merciful. This adds a pericope-level enclosure relation and does not translate the focus verb as veil, withdrawal, or literal trespass.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel support names the branch set and its spatial relation, and every retained carrier lands on supplied 19:16, 19:17, 19:18, or 19:22 surface evidence.

findings.title: Speech reconstitutes privacy
findings.claim: After withdrawal and screening are followed by an embodied human-form appearance, Mary's refuge utterance becomes a portable boundary: speech repairs privacy when spatial privacy no longer secures the encounter.
findings.mechanism: The 19:16 carrier establishes chosen distance, the 19:17 screen blocks access before a human form appears, and the focus refuge form addresses the newly present figure as the source from whom protection is sought. Their contact changes the focus from generic protection from a stranger to a spoken reconstitution of distance.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the sentence as an act that redraws a boundary in the encounter, while the spatial setting remains recoverable underneath it.
findings.containment: The privacy-breach language describes Mary's experience of the arrangement, not an allegation that the figure literally trespassed. The ordinary request for refuge remains intact; unresolved HFT branches are attributed rather than given invented lexical glosses.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace is exact, pericope-complete, and coordinate-consistent, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and its human-form branch remains unresolved.

findings.title: Mercy is followed by accountable disclosure
findings.claim: The invocation of the Merciful is followed by accountable identification, a gift without exchange, purity, and a later naming of the outcome as mercy; refuge therefore makes intelligible disclosure part of protection and permits an apparent threat to be reclassified without erasing the initial alarm.
findings.mechanism: The focus divine name carries the protective relation, the reply identifies messenger and mission, the promised son is given without counterpayment and called pure, and 19:21 repeats the mercy root for the outcome. These carriers contact the focus invocation as a sequence in which protection first secures an intelligible account and then opens a different reading of the encounter.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the answer to the refuge request is speech and identification before the narrative advances: protection changes what the presence can be understood to be.
findings.containment: The primary invocation of the Merciful remains the ground. The later mercy may name the child or sign rather than the encounter itself, so the finding does not declare that Mary's initial alarm was mistaken.

epistemic.reason: All HFT anchors and roles are exact and supplied within the pericope, but the reader identity is legacy_unbound and the non-focus branch descriptors are unresolved.

findings.containment: The focus still says that Mary spoke. The later silence may be ritual as well as tactical, and the finding does not choose between those readings; it records how the sequence reallocates speech.

findings.title: Conditional piety and performative creation
findings.claim: The focus condition tests whether an existing moral state is present, while the later divine saying follows determination and brings being into occurrence; human speech can summon piety into conduct, whereas the supplied later sequence attributes creation to divine performative power.
findings.mechanism: The focus saying, conditional being, and self-protective piety form a human address that asks conduct to manifest an existing state. In 19:35, determination precedes divine saying and the imperative and resultant forms move through being and coming-to-be. The repeated speech-and-being contact changes the focus condition from a merely descriptive clause into an ethical test against the later creation sequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the force of the open condition: the address calls for restraint to become visible without treating the human utterance as able to create that state.
findings.containment: The focus remains a conditional description of the addressee's piety. The later relation may be a broad birth-context echo rather than a deliberate contrast in speech acts, and no divine-creation force is assigned to Mary's words.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT trace supplies the focus and 19:35 coordinates and the changed grammatical relation, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and the determination branch is attributed.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: Determination and divine saying supply the authority and speech that precede the resultant occurrence.
branch_activations.activation: The grouped being carriers contact the focus copular condition through the changed order and agency of the later sequence.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus condition is sharpened as a state-test beside a separate movement that brings being into occurrence.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus copula is not treated as the later imperative.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyi oldurmak, onun gerçekleşmesini sağlama yönünde ettirgen bir uzantıdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The imperative and resultant forms carry the extension from being to causing occurrence.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The decisive determination and performative divine saying provide the causative agency.
branch_activations.activation: The causative extension contacts the focus being carrier and makes the difference between testing a state and bringing a state or thing into occurrence explicit.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Human speech in the focus asks for conduct; the later divine saying is paired with an occurrence-making force.
branch_activations.boundary: This specialization is retained only for the supplied 19:35 forms and is not projected onto the focus.

findings.title: Refuge carries a maternal-enclosure resonance
findings.claim: The focus refuge and Merciful name also carry a contained maternal-enclosure resonance: later pregnancy, labor, and birth make guarding and interior containment perceptible around the focus without replacing its ordinary protective reading.
findings.mechanism: The focus refuge and divine-name carriers meet the 19:22 pregnancy carrier, the 19:23 labor carrier, and the 19:33 birth carrier. That sequence supplies an interior-to-emergence movement, so refuge can be heard as clinging, containing, and guarding across the narrative's movement into birth.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices an embodied enclosure image beneath the invocation: protection can hold an interior life through the transition toward emergence.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory lexical resonance of enclosure and close guarding, not the translation of the refuge verb or divine name. The HFT reader identity is legacy_unbound, and unresolved branches remain attributed.

epistemic.reason: The exact outlier trace supplies focus, pregnancy, labor, and birth coordinates and an explicit containment rule, but it is legacy_unbound and two of its maternal branches have no registered descriptor.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir dişinin doğumdan hemen sonraki ilk günlerde içinde bulunduğu özel durumu adlandırır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus refuge form carries the HFT-attributed maternal-guarding association.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Pregnancy and labor supply the bodily sequence that makes a guarded maternal state live.
branch_activations.activation: The focus refuge contacts the pregnancy-to-labor sequence as a form of close guarding around vulnerable emergence.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Refuge gains a contained maternal guarding undertone while remaining refuge.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus verb is not translated as a postpartum female or as birth.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Dişi bedenindeki bu iç organ, yavrunun oluşup geliştiği yer ve onu karın içinde taşıyan kap işlevindedir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus Merciful name carries the HFT-attributed womb-as-containing-house association.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Pregnancy and labor provide an interior container and its transition toward emergence.
branch_activations.activation: The divine-name carrier contacts the embodied pregnancy sequence, overlaying mercy with protected enclosure.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The protective name can hold a maternal interior image alongside its ordinary divine mercy reading.
branch_activations.boundary: The divine name is not lexically reduced to an anatomical organ.

branch_activations.carrier: The exact HFT-attributed pregnancy occurrence supplies internal carrying and containment.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The two focus carriers name refuge and the protecting Merciful relation.
branch_activations.activation: The pregnancy carrier gives the focus enclosure resonance an embodied interior in which protection can be pictured.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus boundary can be perceived as containing vulnerable life before emergence.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent branch gloss or facet is supplied for this carrier.

branch_activations.carrier: The exact HFT-attributed labor occurrence supplies the bodily transition out of protected enclosure.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Pregnancy and the focus refuge establish the enclosure that labor changes.
branch_activations.activation: Labor contacts the focus refuge through the movement from holding an interior to bringing it toward emergence.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The maternal-enclosure resonance includes transition, not only static shelter.
branch_activations.boundary: This remains attributed evidence and does not invent a branch gloss.

branch_activations.carrier: The exact HFT-attributed birth occurrence completes the supplied maternal sequence.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Pregnancy and labor have already established internal carrying and emergence, while the focus refuge supplies the protective return.
branch_activations.activation: Birth contacts the focus enclosure resonance by completing the movement from guarded interior to visible life.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus protection remains perceptible across the narrative's movement into birth.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not claim a surah-wide maternal system or a lexical birth sense for the focus.

findings.title: A tremor can sound beneath the saying
findings.claim: The ordinary saying can carry a contained tremor beneath it: the immediately preceding human-form presentation gives the focus speech an affective bodily alarm, so the boundary is articulated through alarm as well as through words.
findings.mechanism: The focus saying carrier is paired with the exact HFT-attributed presentation and visible-human-form carriers in 19:17. Their contact changes the speech tag from detached narration into a possible acoustic undertone of fear or anger while the ordinary saying remains the surface act.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear Mary's words as controlled speech under pressure, without having to replace the saying with a different verb.
findings.containment: This is exploratory and form-distant. It must remain an affective or acoustic undertone; the focus saying is not translated as 'she trembled,' and the unresolved carriers receive no invented gloss.

epistemic.reason: The outlier trace names exact 19:17 and 19:18 carriers and an explicit containment rule, but the source is legacy_unbound and two branch identities are unresolved.

branch_activations.facet_statement: İnsan bedeninde beliren titreme, ürperti veya istemsiz silkiniş halidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus saying carries the attributed bodily tremor as an undertone beneath audible speech.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The sudden presentation and visible human form immediately precede the saying.
branch_activations.activation: The focus saying contacts the two presentation carriers at the point where an alarming presence becomes bodily perceptible.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The spoken boundary can be heard as controlled speech under physical alarm.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus saying remains speech; this facet is an undertone, not a replacement translation.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Titremenin belirleyici nedeni korku ya da öfkedir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus saying carries the attributed fear-or-anger cause of the bodily tremor.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The sudden human-form presentation supplies the immediate confrontation that can activate fear or anger.
branch_activations.activation: The affective cause contacts the focus speech through the preceding embodied confrontation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The saying may be heard as deliberately controlled language under fear or anger.
branch_activations.boundary: The packet does not choose fear over anger and does not change the focus verb into a tremor verb.

branch_activations.activation: The presentation carrier gives the focus speech an immediate interpersonal confrontation beneath its ordinary narrative function.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The possible tremor is grounded in a sudden arrival rather than added as free poetic emotion.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent branch gloss or facet is supplied.

branch_activations.carrier: The exact HFT-attributed visible-human-form occurrence gives the alarm an immediate perceptual object.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The sudden presentation carrier and the focus saying place the bodily object directly before the response.
branch_activations.activation: Visible embodiment contacts the focus speech and makes an affective undertone materially connected to the scene.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The words can be heard as responding to a bodily perceived presence.
branch_activations.boundary: This is attributed contextual evidence and does not establish the visitor's intent or a verified branch gloss.

friction_notes: No staged reader responses or reader walks are supplied in the packet; before-and-after language is therefore limited to the focus floor, supplied connection rows, and exact HFT changed_reading fields.

All seven HFT records are legacy_unbound. Exact coordinate-consistent traces are retained, while unresolved branch citations remain attributed with null gloss and facet rather than receiving invented lexical identities.

The explicitly added external ayat 1:2-1:7 were reviewed as a quarantined overlay. The repeated mercy material in 1:3 adds no independent changed reading beyond the native/pericope mercy findings, and 1:2 and 1:4-1:7 supply no specific focus-return carrier; no external overlay finding is admitted.
Non-nominated focus branches have root membership and surface occurrences but no supplied independent trigger or changed reader payoff; root membership alone does not activate them.
